evidence.quote: in light of the heightened uncertainties abroad and a slightly softer expected path for inflation, the Committee judged it appropriate to wait for more evidence
Compared with the projections made in June, many FOMC participants lowered somewhat their paths for the federal funds rate, including estimates of the longer-run normal level.
Accordingly, the Committee anticipates that inflation will remain quite low in the coming months.
The economy has been performing well, and we expect it to continue to do so.
These developments may restrain U.S. economic activity somewhat and are likely to put further downward pressure on inflation in the near term.
So, yes, October remains a possibility.

parsed.rationale: The Committee held off on an expected liftoff citing global risks and softer inflation, and lowered projected rate paths, though it kept a 2015 hike in play and described the domestic economy as strong. The net signal is a moderate dovish delay rather than outright easing.
